findings.location: Section 6 (F), paragraph beginning 'The vocabulary is in use too': 'Only metrology-proper terms (measurand, GUM uncertainty budget, traceability) are unused for LLM confidence, and the two formal metrology papers treat classifiers'

findings.evidence: research/positioning/w4/VERDICTS.md (F Q1 row; Challenge resolutions 'F Q1 metrology-proper vocabulary: Accepted'); research/positioning/w4/parts/critic-A/CHALLENGES.md lines 213-219; vault note trace-a-metrologically-grounded-engineering-frameworkfor-trustworthy-agentic-ai
findings.recommendation: Replace the 'unused' claim with a statement that metrology-proper terms are already applied to LLM stated-confidence calibration at conceptual depth (cite 2604.26671, preprint, April 2026, Sec 1 and Sec 10, and TRACE [[trace-a-metrologically-grounded-engineering-frameworkfor-trustworthy-agentic-ai]]); state that any exposition using 'measurand' or 'readout' must cite them. Keep the sentence that unused-or-not, vocabulary is not a contribution.

findings.issue: The draft never mentions TRIAGE 2605.13414 (concurrent, full text, Sec 3, Eq. 1 to 3), which already normalizes self-directed budget allocation on LiveCodeBench between a random-permutation reference and a knapsack oracle, so the random-to-oracle comparator design on code is published and the residual must be restated as the VERDICTS resolution requires.
findings.evidence: research/positioning/w4/VERDICTS.md L3 Q1/Q4/Q5 row and Challenge resolutions ('Accepted as restatement'); research/positioning/w4/parts/critic-A/CHALLENGES.md lines 116-119
findings.recommendation: Insert a sentence in Section 4.2 acknowledging TRIAGE as the closest occupant on the comparator side (random-permutation to knapsack-oracle normalization of a model's self-written token-budget plan on LiveCodeBench), and restate the residual so it names the gate (elicited verbal or probe confidence) and the unit (execution budget per candidate, matched-budget per-item routing), not the comparator design. Add TRIAGE to the L3 row of the Section 8 table and to the Section 7.3 occupant table (concurrent).

findings.location: Section 5, paragraph beginning 'Three residuals survive': 'Targeted repair versus matched-budget regeneration (Q2) is NARROW: Olausson et al. find ... and the targeted-repair papers lack the matched arm'
findings.issue: The draft omits 2609.00854 (concurrent, ABSTRACT-ONLY), a placebo-controlled study where spectrum-based localization plus infilling loses to blind resampling at matched attempts (3:40, p = 3.0 x 10^-9) across three 26-32B models, and Verma 2607.26117 (full text in vault) where blind resampling beats or ties execution-feedback repair on MBPP+; both shrink the Q2 residual and lower the prior that confidence-guided targeted repair wins.
findings.evidence: research/positioning/w4/VERDICTS.md L4 Q2 row ('NARROW (residual shrinks)'); critic-A/CHALLENGES.md lines 192-194; vault note try-again-dont-look-backblind-resampling-outperforms-self-repair-in-small-code-m
findings.recommendation: Add a sentence that matched-budget localization-versus-resampling with a random-span placebo is now published with a negative result (2609.00854, ABSTRACT-ONLY, flagged as such), and cite [[try-again-dont-look-backblind-resampling-outperforms-self-repair-in-small-code-m]] for the anchoring effect of conditioning on a failed attempt. Restate the residual as only that localization comes from the model's own per-requirement confidence, and note the prior that it wins is lower. Update the L4 Q2 row in Section 8 to 'NARROW (residual shrinks)' with 2609.00854, and amend Section 1.1's claim that NeuroSym-Cal is 'the one load-bearing record' that is ABSTRACT-ONLY.

findings.location: Section 4.3, opening: 'No fetched record measures stated confidence before and after the model sees a failing test on its own program'; and Section 9.3 Rank 3
findings.issue: The draft presents the update-after-failure component as CLEAN (provisional) without naming the near neighbors the VERDICTS resolution says must be read before any novelty sentence: LADDER 2610.34737 (now in vault in full text; self-assessment under unreliable feedback, with a HumanEval extension) and 2610.19226 (Agentic Self-Awareness, reconsideration of stated feasibility after a challenge on Terminal-Bench).
findings.evidence: research/positioning/w4/VERDICTS.md Challenge resolutions ('Leads to read before any novelty sentence: LADDER 2610.34737 and 2610.19226'); critic-A/CHALLENGES.md line 137; vault note ladder-diagnosing-domain-level-self-assessment-under-noisy-feedback
findings.recommendation: Add a sentence naming LADDER [[ladder-diagnosing-domain-level-self-assessment-under-noisy-feedback]] as the closest analogue to the spurious-failure arm (unreliable interaction feedback, including HumanEval, but domain-level self-assessment rather than per-program confidence after a failing test) and 2610.19226 as a coding-adjacent reconsideration probe on task feasibility; state that both must be read in full before a novelty claim for Rank 3.

findings.location: Executive summary: 'Every code comparison that scores a probe against the model's own confidence within problem on self-generated samples finds a tie or a small, model-dependent margin'; Section 3.3 opening: 'all tie or favor the readout'
findings.issue: The draft's own Section 3.3 exceptions paragraph and the Campos full text contradict 'all tie or favor the readout': for gpt-oss in distribution the trained methods reach 0.69-0.78 within-problem AUROC, and a causally localized probe stays 0.09 AUROC ahead of output confidence for Qwen3-Coder under language shift.
findings.evidence: which-signals-of-code-correctness-survive-distribution-shift-hidden-state-and-ca (Sec VI-C: 'The trained methods reach higher within-problem AUROCs of 0.69-0.78 only for gpt-oss in distribution, but lose this advantage under shift')
findings.recommendation: Qualify the Section 3.3 opening so it says the comparisons tie or favor the readout under shift and on the small diffusion and autoregressive samples, with one in-distribution exception (gpt-oss) where trained internal methods lead within problem. Keep the executive-summary wording 'small, model-dependent margin' but drop 'Every ... finds a tie'. Also reconcile the count ('Three code comparisons' while only Miglani and Campos are described).
